# The provenance file on Thémis

*The provenance file for Thémis. Nothing here is unsourced; that is what the file is for.*

## Provenance

**1. The attestation.** **Θέμις** — "A Titaness, the personification of divine order, law, and established custom; a consort of Zeus and mother of the Seasons (Horae) and the Fates (Moirai).". On record: LSJ, Beekes, Etymological Dictionary of Greek, Hesiod, Theogony 132–136, 901–906, Aeschylus, Eumenides 1–8.

**2. The preserved evidence.** **e → é** (Short epsilon) — absent from the ASCII form *themis*, present in the restoration, verifiable against the sources above.

**3. The narrative record.** **The Titaness Who Married Order to Power** — Hesiod enrolls Thémis among the twelve Titans — a daughter of Ouranos and Gaia born at the very beginning of the ordered cosmos (Theogony 132–136) — and then gives her the most consequential marriage of the succession.  Zeus 'lay with Themis, who bore him the Horae: Good Order (Eunomía), Justice (Díkē), and flourishing Peace (Eirḗnē), who watch over the works of mortal men; and the Moirai, to whom wise Zeus gave the greatest honor' (Theogony 901–906). **The Keeper of the Oracle** — The Pythia opens Aeschylus' Eumenides with a genealogy of her own altar: 'first, in this prayer, I honor Earth, the eldest of the gods, who brought me forth; then Themis, for she, they say, was the next to hold this seat, her daughter as she was; and third, with Themis' good will and none by force, another Titan, Phoebe...  gave it as a birthday gift to Phoebus' (1–8).

**4. The physical record.** Pausanias records an altar of Themis among the Elean altars in the Altis at Olympia (5.14), one of the few fixed points of her cult; she was worshipped chiefly in company — with the Horae, at the assembly-seat — rather than alone. Her true monument is theatrical: the opening speech of Aeschylus' Eumenides (458 BCE), performed before the very rock of the Areopagus, makes her the first keeper of Delphi. Vase painters show her occasionally among the assembled gods — at the wedding of Peleus and Thetis, in divine councils — recognizable by her modest bearing among the more flamboyant figures. The cult of 'the way things are done' leaves modest remains; which is, perhaps, exactly right.

**5. The current holding.** The temple at [/themis/](/themis/), classified Tier 2. One decisive feature survives — a single, honest mark — which places the restoration in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

**6. The documented resonances.** **Maritime, Shipping & Ocean Industries**, **Legal, Justice & Compliance**, **Philosophy, Ethics & Standards** — seats argued and weighted in the [pattern atlas](/patterns/), read through the myths in this temple's [Resonance File](/themis/blog/resonance/).

**7. The primary sources.** [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the library this file answers to, open at the [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/).

**8. The continuing record.** Every courthouse statue of a robed woman with scales descends from Thémis — filtered through Justitia and the Renaissance, but unmistakably the Titaness who made order divine.  Her name passed directly into modern institutions: asteroid 24 Themis (1853), NASA's THEMIS mission (2007), and countless law reviews and legal institutes.
